description:
Edits to the open presentation (a file whose kind is SLIDE). Edits apply live for anyone viewing the presentation. Requires edit access. Call as {"action": "<name>", "params": {...}}.

Read the presentation first (slide_read deck_outline or read_deck) to get slide and shape ids. Every edit returns what it wrote (new ids, placeholder shapes, z-order) and saved: false if it hadn't been confirmed yet (it is still applied).

Text content is Markdown by default (paragraphs, - bullets with two-space nesting, 1. numbering, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, <u>, <sup>, <sub>, links), or ProseMirror JSON with format: "json". Lengths are EMU unless units is "in" or "pt". Layouts: title, obj (Title and Content, the default), secHead, twoObj, twoTxTwoObj, titleOnly, blank, objTx, picTx — names or labels.

Actions:
• add_slide(layout?, after_slide_id?, index?, title?, body?, notes?, format?) — Add a slide and fill its title/body placeholders. Returns the slide id and its shapes.
• delete_slides(slide_ids) / duplicate_slides(slide_ids) / move_slide(slide_id, index).
• update_slide(slide_id, layout?, background?, transition?, hidden?, notes?, format?) — null clears background or transition; a new layout keeps placeholder text. reset_slide(slide_id) — Put placeholders back where the layout has them (PowerPoint's Reset).
• set_text(slide_id, shape_id? | placeholder?, cell?, content, format?) — Replace a shape's text; placeholder is "title", "subtitle" or "body"; cell: {row, col} for a table.
• format_text(slide_id, shape_id? | placeholder?, cell?, paragraphs?, match?, case_sensitive?, whole_word?, regex?, style) — Format text in place without retyping it. style: {bold?, italic?, underline?, strike?, superscript?, subscript?, font_family?, font_size_pt?, color?, highlight?, caps: "all" | "small"?, letter_spacing_pt?, link?, align: "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify"?, line_height?, space_before_pt?, space_after_pt?, indent_pt?, list: "none" | "bullet" | "number"?}; null clears a property. Scope with paragraphs (zero-based indices as read_deck lists them) and/or match (only the matching text; paragraph properties apply to paragraphs containing a match). Omit cell on a table to format every cell.
• add_shape(slide_id, shape, geometry?, xfrm?, units?, name?, text?, format?, fill?, line?, body_pr?, src?, rows?, cols?, cells?) — shape: "text_box", "shape" (with geometry e.g. rect, ellipse, rightArrow), "connector", "picture" (src data/https URL) or "table" (rows/cols or cells text). Omit xfrm for a centered default size.
• update_shape(slide_id, shape_id, xfrm?, units?, name?, geometry?, fill?, line?, body_pr?, hidden?, descr?, src?, crop?) — xfrm may be partial; null removes fill, line, descr or crop. src and crop ({l?, t?, r?, b?} fractions of each edge) are for pictures.
• delete_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids) / duplicate_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids) / reorder_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids, move: "front" | "back" | "forward" | "backward").
• align_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids, alignment: "left" | "center" | "right" | "top" | "middle" | "bottom") — One shape aligns to the slide, several to each other. distribute_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids, axis: "horizontal" | "vertical") — Space three or more shapes evenly.
• group_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids) — Group two or more shapes; they then share a group_id. ungroup_shapes(slide_id, shape_ids) — Dissolve the groups those shapes belong to.
• edit_table(slide_id, shape_id, op: "insert_row" | "delete_row" | "insert_column" | "delete_column", at).
• format_table(slide_id, shape_id, style?, first_row?, band_row?, col_widths?, row_heights?, units?, cells?, cell_fill?, cell_anchor?) — Table style (mediumStyle2Accent1, lightStyle1, themedStyle1Accent1, noStyle), header row and banding, one width per column / one height per row (the table resizes to fit), and fill or text anchor (t|ctr|b) for the given cells (default all). merge_cells(slide_id, shape_id, from, to) / split_cell(slide_id, shape_id, cell) — Merge the rectangle of cells (their text joins the top-left cell) or split a merged cell again.
• find_replace(find, replace, case_sensitive?, whole_word?, regex?) — Replace text throughout; replacements keep the formatting of the text they replace.
• update_presentation(slide_size_preset?, slide_size?, units?, scale_content?, theme?, footer?) — slide_size_preset is "16:9" | "4:3" | "16:10", slide_size is a custom {cx, cy}; shapes scale to the new size unless scale_content is false. theme: {name?, colors?: {dk1, lt1, dk2, lt2, accent1–accent6, hlink, folHlink}, fonts?: {major, minor}} merges into the current theme. footer: {show_slide_number?, show_date?, footer_text?} or null to remove.
• add_comment(slide_id, shape_id?, x?, y?, units?, text) — Start a comment thread, anchored to a shape when shape_id is given. reply_to_comment(comment_id, text) / update_comment(comment_id, text?, resolved?) / delete_comments(comment_ids).
• batch(operations) — Up to 100 edits as one all-or-nothing change: {"operations": [{"action": "<name>", "params": {...}}, ...]}. Ids created by earlier operations aren't available to later ones in the same batch.

action.description: Action to perform: add_slide, delete_slides, move_slide, duplicate_slides, update_slide, reset_slide, set_text, format_text, add_shape, update_shape, delete_shapes, duplicate_shapes, reorder_shapes, align_shapes, distribute_shapes, group_shapes, ungroup_shapes, edit_table, format_table, merge_cells, split_cell, find_replace, update_presentation, add_comment, reply_to_comment, update_comment, delete_comments, or batch

params.description: Parameters for the action (see tool description). For batch: {operations: [{action, params}, ...]}

name: slide_write
